title: Session boundary compaction & late-fragment attribution for accurate token credits
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Streaming requests that are split across multiplexed transports or experience out-of-order delivery are currently producing transient double-credits or lost credits in the metering pipeline. The root cause is inconsistent session seam handling across the ingress layer, fragment compaction in the preprocessor, and the crediting window in the aggregator. Consequence: customers observe unexpected invoice deltas or quota jumps when clients reconnect or when proxy reorder happens.

Goal: Implement a robust session-boundary compaction and 'late-fragment attribution' algorithm that deterministically attributes token credits to the canonical session snapshot (by session id + monotonic chunk index) and deduplicates overlapping fragments while preserving low-latency streaming semantics and accurate per-route accounting.
design_notes:
1) Introduce a compacted-session record in the preprocessor that keeps a short-lived sliding window (configurable, default 15s) of seen fragment indexes and their canonical attribution. 2) Attribute late fragments to the last accepted checkpoint instead of creating a new credit event; late fragments that only extend an already-credited suffix should be dropped. 3) For out-of-order fragments with overlapping token ranges, apply deterministic ownership rules: prefer the fragment with the lowest transport-timestamp and then smallest transport-seq if tie. 4) Expose an opt-in feature flag (metering.compaction.v2) for staged rollout. 5) Provide a migration job that reprocesses buffered session snapshots for the last 7 days to backfill missing credits if rollback is necessary.

Alternative considered: Use strict server-side causal ordering (hold fragments until sequence contiguous). Rejected because it increases tail latency and impacts SLOs for low-latency apps.
implementation_plan:
- Phase 1: Add compacted-session data structure and deterministic owner selection (2s sprint).
- Phase 2: Implement dedupe/drop rules and integrate with credit-aggregation (2s sprint).
- Phase 3: Add instrumentation and alerting; QA harness for interleaved streams (1s sprint).
- Phase 4: Gradual rollout behind feature flag + migration job; monitor billing diff and quota anomalies (2s).

Key modules touched: ingress preprocessor, streaming-router, metering-aggregator, billing-validator. Expected code changes in: repo/ingress, repo/metering, repo/billing-validator.

Estimated PRs: ~4 (preprocessor, aggregator, migration job, integration tests).
acceptance_criteria:
- Deterministic attribution: For synthetic test harness with out-of-order fragments, token counts match a ground-truth aggregator in 100% of runs.
- No revenue regression: Rolling 24h billing diff <= 0.1% for test workspace during canary.
- Latency SLO: P95 token latency change <= +5ms after feature enabled.
- Alerts: New anomaly detection fires when token attribution delta > 0.5% across all customers.
- Rollback safe: Feature flag can be disabled without leaving orphaned credits; migration job is reversible.
qa_steps:
1) Run unit tests for compaction logic; assert deterministic ordering rules.
2) Run integration scenario suite (10k simulated streams with reorder and reconnect) and compare token tallies to golden dataset.
3) Deploy to staging with metering.compaction.v2=true for a subset of orgs; validate billing-compare dashboard.
4) Execute manual blackbox test: interrupt client mid-stream, reconnect with overlapping fragment IDs, verify no duplicate credits.
5) Run migration job on staging backfill; ensure idempotency and no double-credit on repeated runs.
metrics_and_queries:
- billing.compare.delta_by_org (SQL): SELECT org, SUM(new_credits - old_credits) / SUM(old_credits) as pct FROM billing_compare WHERE window='24h' GROUP BY org;
- streaming.fragment.latency P95/P99 by transport and region.
- dedupe.rate: count of fragments dropped_by_compaction / total_fragments.
- false_positive_alerts: number of anomaly alerts triggered during canary.

Dashboards to watch: 'Metering — Canary: compaction-v2', 'Billing regressions (last 7d)'.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Over-eager dropping could under-credit customers. Mitigation: Start with conservative window and add tombstone markers; run dual-write compare for 7 days.
Risk: Increased memory in preprocessor due to sliding window. Mitigation: Bounded LRU and TTL; fallback to summarization when memory pressure high.
Risk: Migration complexity causing temporary billing mismatches. Mitigation: Run migration as read-only comparator first, then enable backfill with throttle and dry-run logs.
rollout_plan:
1) Alpha: internal orgs + canary (5% traffic) behind metering.compaction.v2. Monitor for 48h.
2) Beta: Expand to 25% traffic and run migration job in dry-run mode to compute proposed backfill credits.
3) GA: full rollout and enable migration backfill for rolling windows older than 24h.
4) If billing diff > 0.5% aggregate, immediately disable flag and run rollback job to reconcile states.

Communication: notify finance & customer-success 48h before GA; prepare template notes for customers seeing changes.
